sentences.text:
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.

Sri Mohd. Qasim, Advocate submitted that he has filed his power on behalf of the informant which
is taken on record.

2.  Sri Brijesh Kumar, learned AGA apprised the Court that he has received the instructions,
therefore, the instant anticipatory bail application may be finally, disposed off.

3. Heard Sri Amit Daga, learned counsel for the applicants; Sri Mohd. Qasim, learned counsel for the informant and Sri Brijesh Kumar, learned A.G.A. for the State-respondent.
4.

The present anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicants in Case Crime No. 83 of 2023, under Sections 498A, 323, 328 IPC & Section 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Arniya,
District Bulandshahr, with a prayer to enlarge them on anticipatory bail, till the conclusion of trial.

sentences.text: 1 5. FIR of the present case was lodged against the applicants and their family members and according to the FIR marriage of the sister of the informant was performed with the younger brother of the applicant no. 1 and since marriage applicants and their family members tortured her for dowry and on 14.4.2023 victim informed the informant that family members of her husband are torturing her and when he after receiving information arrived at her matrimonial home then found that she was in the hospital.

6. Learned counsel for the applicants submits that on the basis of false allegations applicants have been made accused in the present matter and applicant no. 1 is the Jeth of the victim, while applicant no. 2 is her mother in law and actually matrimonial dispute was pending between both the parties and due to matrimonial dispute victim herself consumed some poisonous substance and thereafter she was admitted to hospital and this fact is even evident from the statement of the doctor Dinesh which has been annexed as annexure-7 to the affidavit which clearly shows that victim herself informed the doctor that she consumed some poisonous substance.
7.

He further submitted that initially FIR of the present case was lodged only under sections 323,
498A IPC and D.P. Act and on 7.7.2023 applicants were enlarged on anticipatory bail for offences under sections 498A, 323 IPC and D.P. Act till submission of the police report under section 173(2)
Cr.P.C. but during investigation offence under section 328 IPC was added and when during investigation, applicants applied for bail for offence under section 328 IPC then on 26.10.23, they were enlarged on interim anticipatory bail till 8.11.2023 but in the meantime on 7.11.2023, charge sheet has been submitted and thereafter anticipatory bail application filed by the applicants was dismissed.
8.

He further submitted that applicants never misused the liberty of anticipatory bail granted to them during investigation and now charge sheet has been submitted and therefore, custodial interrogation of the applicants is not required.
9. He further submitted that applicants are having apprehensions that if they will appear before the court concerned then they will be sent to jail.
10. He further submitted that applicants are not having any previous criminal history to their credit.

11. Per contra, learned AGA as well as learned counsel for the informant opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail and submitted that applicant no. 1 is the Jeth of the victim and applicant no. 2 is her mother in law and both badly tortured her alongwith other family members including husband of the victim and they also provided some poisonous substance to her and due to that victim had to remain in hospital for considerable period of time.

12. They further submitted that when the second statement of the doctor was recorded during investigation by the Investigating Officer then he categorically stated that it was a case of poisoning and therefore, applicants are not entitled to be released on anticipatory bail.
13. I have heard learned counsel both the sides and perused the record of the case.

sentences.text:
Applicant nos. 1 and 2 are Jeth and mother in law of the victim, respectively and initially FIR of the present case was lodged under sections 323, 498A IPC and D.P. Act and during investigation,
court concerned released them on anticipatory bail for offence under sections 323, 498A IPC and DP Act till submission of the police report under section 173(2) IPC but it appears that during investigation, offence under sections 328 IPC was added and thereafter, when applicants applied for anticipatory bail before the court concerned then they were enlarged on interim anticipatory bail but in the meantime, charge sheet has been submitted and thereafter anticipatory bail application moved by the applicants was dismissed.
15. There is no allegation that during investigation applicants misused the liberty of anticipatory bail.

16. As far as merit of the case is concerned, only general allegations have been leveled against the applicants and other accused persons including husband of the victim and according to the victim,
all the accused persons provided tea to her and after consumption of the same, she fell ill.

17. However, victim remained in hospital for considerable period of time and according to second statement of the doctor Dinesh who providing medical treatment to the victim, it was a case of poisoning but there is no evidence on record which can show that applicants are the persons who either mixed poison in the tea of the victim or administered poison to her.
18. Further, from the first statement of doctor Dinesh recorded during investigation it reflects that victim informed him that she herself consumed some poisonous substance.

19. Further after submission of the charge sheet custodial interrogation of the applicants does not appear to be necessary and apprehension of custody raised by the applicants cannot be ruled out and applicants are not having any previous criminal history to their credit.

20. Therefore, considering the fact and circumstances discussed above and observation made by the Apex Court in the Case of [Aman Preet Singh Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation, (2022) 13 Supreme Court Cases 764], in my view, applicants are entitled to be enlarged on anticipatory bail in this case, till conclusion of trial.

entities.text: Aman Preet Singh Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation, (2022) 13 Supreme Court Cases 764]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 21. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant anticipatory bail application of the applicants is allowed.

24. It is made clear that observations made in granting anticipatory bail to the applicants shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
